purpose: Candidate-visible identity semantics. The examples are authoritative for this trial but do not prescribe an implementation.
global_rules: A universal product is a marketed model or generation shared across sellers.
A variant is the exact configuration on which price comparison is safe.
Seller, condition, price, availability, and temporary promotions are offer or observation evidence, not product identity.
Price level, discount size, and which configuration is cheaper are never identity evidence.

A total purchase price, monthly installment, trade-in net amount, subscription price, and coupon-conditional amount are different monetary semantics and must not be ranked as if they were interchangeable.
Agreement from records with the same content or syndication origin is correlated evidence, not independent confirmation.
A source may evolve between compatible schema versions; preserve version provenance and quarantine only the record that cannot be safely interpreted.
Identifier equality is evidence at the identifier's semantic scope; a family/style/configurable-offer identifier does not prove exact-variant equality.
Variant-significant dimensions can depend on a product family as well as its broad category.
Unknown structured attributes and explicit exclusions should survive normalization with provenance; a token mentioned as compatible or not included is not positive contents evidence.
Additional hierarchy levels are allowed; evaluation focuses on safe semantic relationships rather than required entity names.
Missing material evidence does not prove equality. Conflicting material evidence normally requires REVIEW.
A manufacturer bundle, retailer-added bundle, multipack, and temporary entitlement can have different identity consequences and must retain provenance.
